confidence_notes: I used 6 web searches: 1 for the RBA rate and 5 for prices. The price searches returned aggregated cost-of-living sources (Expatistan, MyLifeElsewhere, Wise, Traveltables, and a 2026 guide), all crowd-sourced or estimated. Many pages were undated or a few years old. Prices were in RON, which I converted at roughly 4.4 RON per USD from general knowledge, not from a searched rate. Restaurant meals: inexpensive meal about 50 RON, mid-range meal for two about £49 or €59. Coffee: cappuccino about 13-15 RON. Cocktail: about 22-38 RON, with a club listing at 23 RON. Draft beer: pint about 15 RON, and a 2026 guide gives 8-15 RON for a local beer in a restaurant. I found no direct menu price for wine by the glass, so I inferred it from bottle prices (about 43 RON retail) and the usual restaurant glass-to-beer relationship. That anchor is the least certain, along with the cocktail. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and the city context. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any booking pages or listings, so those four are the least certain overall.
comparable_city_reasoning: Cluj-Napoca is Romania's second-largest city and a university and tech hub. Sources put its restaurant prices about 15-25% above the national average and slightly below Bucharest. Accommodation is benchmarked against mid-priced Central and Eastern European cities such as Brasov and Sibiu, with a modest premium for Cluj's demand from tourists, events and business travel.
